rows.answer: Section 4 imposes income tax on the taxable income of every person who has taxable income for the tax year. The tax is levied at the rate or rates specified in Division I or Division II of Part I of the First Schedule, as applicable to the taxpayer, for tax year 2027 onward.

rows.answer: For tax year 2027 onwards, the surcharge under Section 4AB is levied at a rate of ten percent of the income tax imposed under Division I of Part I of the First Schedule [1]. It applies only when an individual’s or association’s taxable income exceeds Rs 10 million, and no surcharge is payable on income chargeable under the head “Salary” [1].

rows.answer: For tax year 2027, a banking company whose income exceeds Rs 150 million is subject to a super tax of 10 % of that income.

rows.answer: For tax year 2027, a person who is not a banking company, not a fertilizer seller and not a Fifth‑Schedule person and whose income exceeds Rs 500 million is subject to a super tax of 8 % of that income.[1]
